title: Geolocation
description: Origin and destination locality codes under a DECLARED geocode standard — where an order originates and terminates. Composed for ANY modality and BOTH physical and digital value chains: a shipment route (cell-grid codes: geohash, H3, S2, Open Location Code), a service jurisdiction or digital-delivery territory (jurisdiction codes: ISO 3166-1/-2, UN/LOCODE; endpoint territory in digital chains is evidenced per RFC 8805/9632 geofeeds). The standard is the source of truth — referenced, never restated; the axis is OPEN (any standard, existing or future). Carries no physical-shipment assumption; mass and volume live in the elective figaro-cargo clause.

fields.name: geocodeStandard
fields.label: Geocode standard
fields.description: How the two location codes below are written. Geohash is the usual choice and the built-in default; H3, S2, and Open Location Code work too, and any standard you name is accepted.

fields.name: geocoder
fields.label: Geocoder
fields.description: A Nominatim-compatible geocoding endpoint the parties resolve typed locations through when producing the origin/destination codes — a DESIGN fill: the designer pins it when tailoring the assembly, so every party to the deal resolves through the SAME service instead of whatever each client happened to configure. Optional because jurisdiction-grade standards (iso3166-1/-2, unlocode) need no geocoder at all; cell-grid standards (geohash, h3, s2, olc) typically name one. An OPEN axis like the standard itself: any https endpoint speaking the declared standard's resolution is valid.

fields.name: origin
fields.description: Where the order starts, as a location code in the standard above. Give the neighbourhood, never the door: a geohash of six characters or fewer. The exact address travels privately to the other party at hand-off; it is never written to the chain.
fields.label: Origin

fields.name: destination
fields.description: Where the order ends, as a location code in the standard above. Your phone can fill it from its location. Give the neighbourhood, never the door: a geohash of six characters or fewer. The exact address travels privately to the other party at hand-off; it is never written to the chain.
fields.label: Destination
